clue.text: Such a scare may be so headily uplifting

definitions.text: Such a scare may be so headily uplifting

parts.words: Such a scare may be so headily uplifting
parts.note: a fright so intense it lifts the strands on top of your head, read literally as something lifting the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Headily uplifting' sounds like praise for an exhilarating experience, but read literally it is something that makes what grows on your head stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying experience is described idiomatically as making your locks stand on end, so the clue's literal uplift points to that phrase.

clue.text: Where stars may be left in sacred forest

indicators.note: the word left is placed in the middle of the word for sacred

parts.note: sacred means holy
a forest is a wood

explanation.surface: A mystic grove where the stars have been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests the night sky, but they are film stars, and the district is in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Los Angeles district is the home of the American film industry and its celebrities.

clue.text: Charges up motorway and crashes, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: crashes signals the letters of upset are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver is charged after going up the motorway and crashing, leaving everyone upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MI to IM; 'crashes' rearranges UPSET into PUTES. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with something is to attribute or ascribe it to them.

clue.text: Everybody gets up in regret, seeing foul

indicators.note: in places the turned word for everybody within the word for regret

parts.note: to regret is to repent

indicators.note: in a down clue, gets up means the word for everybody rises, so it reads backwards

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: Everyone stands up in remorse at seeing a foul committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' reverses the word for everybody, as the entry runs down. 'Foul' looks like a sporting foul (a noun), but it is the adjective meaning disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellant is disgusting or offensive, exactly what is meant by foul as an adjective.

clue.text: One new place for computer data

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A newly arrived place set aside for storing computer data.
explanation.definitionFit: Data fed into a computer for processing is the term used in computing for what goes in.

clue.text: Ways to support one bearing incursions

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means standing underneath, so the ways go below the other letters

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
N, north, is a compass bearing
ways are roads

explanation.surface: Routes built to support a soldier carrying out raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts ROADS under IN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances into enemy territory, that is, raids or forays.

clue.text: Winds up prisoner and enjoys surroundings

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for prisoner is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lag is British slang for a convict

indicators.note: the surroundings of a word are its first and last letters, enclosing the rest

explanation.surface: A prisoner winds up enjoying his surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAG into GAL; 'surroundings' takes the first and last letters of enjoys, ES. 'Winds up' looks like a phrasal verb but 'Winds' is the definition (strong breezes).
explanation.definitionFit: Gales are very strong breezes, a type of high wind.

clue.text: Student unit in set-back — what a bloomer!

indicators.note: in places the student and unit letters within the turned word for set
set-back says the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: to set something is to put it
L, for learner driver, stands for student
I, the Roman one, is a unit

explanation.surface: A student taking a unit after a setback makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PUT into TUP, and LI goes inside. 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is literally a plant that flowers, and the spring bulb is a classic example.

clue.text: Gently stroked a snooker ball, delighted

parts.note: to tickle is to touch or stroke lightly
the pink is one of the coloured balls in snooker

explanation.surface: A snooker player delicately strokes a ball and is pleased with the shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The pink is one of the coloured balls in snooker, a British cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrilled or very pleased is expressed by the idiom of being stroked into a rosy glow.

clue.text: Item of stationery found in telegraph magazine?

explanation.surface: Something from the desk drawer turns up in the newspaper's weekend supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: an excerpt cut from a newspaper or its magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bent wire fastener for holding sheets together, and also a cutting taken from a newspaper.

clue.text: Producer not producing log

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A film producer fails to come up with a production diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges PRODUCER NOT. 'Log' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to record.
explanation.definitionFit: To log something is to enter it formally in a record or register.

clue.text: Palace ball is rock solid!

explanation.surface: A palace ball is declared a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Crystal Palace is a London football club named after a Victorian exhibition hall; a fortune-teller gazes into a crystal ball; and a crystal is a solid mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: The word precedes Palace and ball in familiar names, and quartz is a mineral of this kind, a solid with an ordered structure.

clue.text: Time operated model found in passage

parts.note: operated, of a machine, means ran
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A clock-operated model is discovered in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage means movement from one place to another, as in goods carried en route.

clue.text: Reel back from winds

indicators.note: back means the word for reel is read from right to left

parts.note: a reel is a spool

explanation.surface: Someone staggers back away from the gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reel' and 'winds' look like verbs of staggering and breezes, but winds is a noun meaning coils.
explanation.definitionFit: Coils or turns of a rope or wire are curls made by winding it.

clue.text: Undertaking by a Danish leader to give access

indicators.note: by means beside, so the undertaking stands next to the other letters
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an undertaking or task is a mission

explanation.surface: A Danish leader promises to allow entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaking' looks like a promise, but it is a task or assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allowed in or granted entry is what it means to gain access.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-roaders have tempers

explanation.surface: Political centrists are bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempers' looks like a noun for bad moods, but it is the verb meaning softens.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrists are people of mild political views, and to temper something is to make it less extreme.

clue.text: Provokes Rita and tries to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the two names and words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone annoys Rita and attempts to alter things.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke someone is to annoy or exasperate them.

clue.text: Pledged to add deceit to list

indicators.note: to list is to lean over, as a ship does, so the letters tilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A promise to include lies on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' means tilt (as a ship lists), signalling an anagram of ADD DECEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledged here means committed or devoted, as in being bound to a cause.

clue.text: Student in campaigns for partial sentences

indicators.note: in places the student letter inside the word for campaigns

parts.note: campaigns are causes
L, for learner driver, stands for student

explanation.surface: A student joins political campaigns, asking for reduced prison terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentences' suggests prison terms, but these are grammatical: parts of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a group of words forming part of a larger grammatical sentence.

clue.text: Form of literature that's not willing to omit the beginning

indicators.note: to omit the beginning means the first letter of the word for not willing is dropped

parts.note: averse means unwilling or opposed

explanation.surface: A literary form that is reluctant to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: AVERSE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is writing arranged in metrical lines, a form of literature distinct from prose.

clue.text: One calls for victory — is it over outside?

indicators.note: outside takes just the outer pair from the word over, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for victory, asking whether the game is over outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One calls' looks like the subject of a shout, but means one who pays a call.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who calls at a house is a guest or caller.

clue.text: Almost suggest worker is a cosmetic addition

indicators.note: almost means the word for suggest is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to suggest is to imply
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A hint that a labourer has had something done to their looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic surgeon may insert something such as silicone under the skin to enhance appearance.

clue.text: Walked quietly with expert on diamonds

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
an ace is an expert
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoed past with a jewellery expert.
explanation.definitionFit: To pace is to walk with regular steps, often back and forth.

clue.text: Follow redhead in queue

indicators.note: in places the head letter of red inside the word for queue

parts.note: a queue or line is a tail
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person tags along in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like a ginger-haired person, but it means the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone secretly is to track or shadow them.

clue.text: Teacher turned to German chap's food

indicators.note: turned means the word for teacher is read backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: The teacher turned to a German man's lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives RIS from SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Italian rice dish, a kind of meal.

clue.text: Get moving for cheap thrills and bitter

parts.note: kicks are cheap thrills, as in doing something for kicks
bitter or sharp means tart

explanation.surface: To get going, one seeks cheap thrills and a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter suggests the British beer, but here it means sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an engine or project going is to give it an initial boost.

clue.text: Bore a child to journalist

parts.note: a tot is a small child
ED, editor, is the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A mother gave birth, handing a child to a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests giving birth (or tedium), but here it means carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Toted means carried, the past of to tote, as bore is the past of to bear.

clue.text: Discuss role played by revelations

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are acted out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Talking over a role in a drama leads to revelations.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing secrets or facts means making disclosures.
